PoMAS Clinical & Dissertation Research Report

Personalised Open Multi-Agent System for Closed-Loop Seizure Early Warning

Candidate: Syed Hussain Ali Zaidi

Supervisor: Dr. Syed Muhammad Usman

Institution: Bahria University, Islamabad (2026)

Database: CHB-MIT Scalp EEG (19 Channels, 256 Hz)

Evaluation Regime: Zero-Leakage Recording & Cluster Disjoint

1. Executive Summary & Thesis Contributions

This clinical report synthesizes the empirical evidence, multi-modal feature representations, explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) attributions, and autonomous multi-agent evaluations developed under the PoMAS framework.

Key Thesis Defense Finding: Raw window-level machine learning produces between 100 and 720 false alarms per hour on noisy scalp EEG streams. By encapsulating models within an autonomous 3-Agent Complex Event Processing (CEP) Orchestrator (Monitoring → Prediction → Alert), false alarms are reduced by 45× to 217× (down to 2–3 alarms/hour) while preserving 100% preictal episode sensitivity across all evaluated patients.

3. Tri-Modal Feature Fusion SOTA & Diagnostic Progression

The PoMAS predictive engine fuses three complementary neuro-electrophysiological representations totaling 1,546 dimensions:

  • Modality 1: Deep Spatial Spectrograms (1,280 dims): Extracted via fine-tuned EfficientNet-B0 from 19-channel log-magnitude STFT transforms.
  • Modality 2: Functional Connectivity (171 dims): Pairwise Pearson correlation matrices capturing inter-electrode hypersynchrony.
  • Modality 3: Canonical Spectral Energy (95 dims): Welch PSD across Delta (0.5–4Hz), Theta (4–8Hz), Alpha (8–13Hz), Beta (13–30Hz), and Gamma (30–50Hz).
Figure 1: Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC).

Figure 4: 4-Model Progression Barchart.

4. Explainable AI (XAI) Clinical Decision Support Panels

To satisfy clinical validation requirements for intensive care and neuro-critical units, each early warning alert is accompanied by an automated 4-quadrant interpretability panel generated via Grad-CAM and input gradient saliency:

Figure 5: XAI Clinical Attribution Panel — Preictal Episode 1 (Recording: chb01_20.edf).
Focal activation is heavily concentrated at electrode pair FP1-F7 in the Theta (4–8 Hz) and Beta (13–30 Hz) bands, providing a 23.8-minute early warning prior to clinical onset.
Figure 6: XAI Clinical Attribution Panel — Preictal Episode 2 (Recording: chb01_26.edf).
Independent confirmation of focal localization at FP1-F7 with 27.8-minute lead time.
Clinical Neurological Validation: The physiological focus identified by PoMAS at FP1-F7 and F7-T7 directly correlates with the patient's verified neurological diagnosis in the CHB-MIT clinical metadata: intractable left fronto-temporal focal onset epilepsy.

6. Scientific Defense Arguments for Examination Committee

Q: "Why is patient-dependent calibration necessary?"

Empirical Evidence: In Patient-Independent models (PRED-PI-01 to 06), Dual-Graph GNN achieved ROC 0.637 on subject chb05, but collapsed to 0.408 on subject chb03. Scalp EEG features are subject-dependent due to individual skull conductivity, electrode impedances, and anatomical seizure foci. Personalised Tri-Modal modeling achieves reliable high performance (ROC 0.868, F1 76.2%).

Q: "Why is raw ML accuracy deceptive?"

Empirical Evidence: In Seizure Detection (DET-01 & DET-03), models scored 78.8% and 69.3% accuracy, but had 0.0% to 2.0% preictal recall. In extreme class imbalance, raw accuracy reflects the majority interictal class. Macro F1, PR-AUC, and episode sensitivity are the only scientifically defensible metrics.

Q: "What is the primary contribution of the multi-agent system?"

Empirical Evidence: Closing the loop between ML inference and clinical triage. Without agents, raw window classification floods clinicians with 100–720 false alarms per hour. The CEP engine's consecutive window debounce and 30-minute refractory lockout suppresses alarms by 45× to 217×, transforming raw predictions into safe, actionable bedside alerts.
